text:
The strongest refutation of Bentham’s felicific calculus is that pleasure and pain are not one homogeneous, cardinally measurable quantity that can be summed across persons and kinds of experience. Without that commensurability, intensity, duration, certainty, propinquity, fecundity, purity, and extent cannot yield a single total that ranks actions. Their inevitability is already assumed by the calculus and leaves it intact.

CONFIDENCE: 74
